questions.prompt: An NMOS has \(V_T = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\). With \(V_{GS} = 0.3\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{DS} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\), which region is it in?
questions.explanation: \(V_{GS} < V_T\): no inversion channel connects source and drain, so ideally \(I_D = 0\) (reader Eq. 8.41).

questions.explanation: On: \(V_{ov} = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\). The channel reaches the drain while \(V_{DS} < V_{ov}\), so it is in triode.

questions.prompt: \(V_T = 0.45\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{GS} = 1.0\ \mathrm{V}\). Above what \(V_{DS}\) (in V) is the device saturated?
questions.explanation: \(V_{DS,sat} = V_{GS} - V_T = 0.55\ \mathrm{V}\). Beyond that the channel pinches off at the drain.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: On the \(I_D\)-\(V_{DS}\) family, what does the dashed parabola mark?
options: Where \(I_D\) is maximum for any bias
questions.explanation: Each curve bends over and goes flat where \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\); since \(I_{D,sat} \propto V_{ov}^2\), those knee points lie on a parabola.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: With \(V_{GS}\) fixed above \(V_T\), you raise \(V_{DS}\) from 0. Which sequence of regions do you see?
options: Triode (nearly linear at first), then saturation
questions.explanation: Near \(V_{DS} = 0\) the channel is a resistor (linear). As \(V_{DS}\) rises toward \(V_{ov}\) the drain end thins and the curve bends; beyond \(V_{ov}\) it saturates.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: An NMOS with its drain tied to its gate (\(V_{DS} = V_{GS}\)) and \(V_T = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\) is biased at \(V_{GS} = 0.95\ \mathrm{V}\). By how many volts does \(V_{DS}\) exceed the saturation boundary?
questions.explanation: \(V_{DS} - (V_{GS} - V_T) = V_T = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\). A diode-connected device is always saturated when on.

questions.prompt: \(V_T = 0.4\ \mathrm{V}\). The source is at 0.2 V, the gate at 1.0 V and the drain at 0.7 V (all to ground). Which region?
questions.explanation: Always use terminal differences: \(V_{GS} = 0.8\), \(V_{DS} = 0.5\). Comparing node voltages to ground directly is a common trap.

questions.prompt: Equivalent saturation test: an NMOS is saturated when the drain is no lower than what?
options: One threshold below the gate: \(V_D \ge V_G - V_T\)
questions.explanation: \(V_{DS} \ge V_{GS} - V_T\) rearranges to \(V_D \ge V_G - V_T\). The drain may sit up to \(V_T\) below the gate and stay saturated.

questions.prompt: On the \(I_D\)-\(V_{GS}\) curve of a saturated NMOS, the current is \(40\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) at \(V_{GS} = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(160\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) at \(V_{GS} = 0.9\ \mathrm{V}\). Assuming the square law, what is \(V_T\) (in V)?
questions.figure_alt: Saturation drain current versus gate-source voltage: zero below threshold V_T, then a parabola in the overdrive.

questions.prompt: Preview of the square law: an NMOS with \(\mu_nC_{ox}W/L = 2\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\) is saturated at \(V_{ov} = 0.25\ \mathrm{V}\). Find \(I_D\) in µA.
questions.figure_alt: Saturation drain current versus gate-source voltage: zero below threshold V_T, then a parabola in the overdrive.

questions.prompt: Preview of triode: near \(V_{DS} = 0\), what does an on NMOS look like between drain and source?
options: A resistor whose conductance is proportional to \(V_{GS} - V_T\)
questions.explanation: The channel is a uniform sheet of inversion charge \(C_{ox}V_{ov}\), so it conducts like a gate-controlled resistor.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: Preview of channel-length modulation: measured saturated curves are not perfectly flat. What makes them rise slightly?
options: The pinch-off point moves toward the source as \(V_{DS}\) grows, shortening the effective channel
The threshold falls with \(V_{DS}\) only in triode
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary. The saturated curves slope upward slightly (channel-length modulation).
